stem: The weekly wages (in Rs) of workers in a factory follow a normal distribution. It is known that 15.87% of workers earn less than Rs 430 per week and 97.72% earn less than Rs 490 per week. Given P(Z < 1) = 0.8413 and P(Z < 2) = 0.9772, what is the standard deviation of weekly wages?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Setting Z = +1 for the lower tail: (490 - 430)/sigma = 2, using mu = 430 directly, gives (490 - 430)/sigma = 2 => sigma = 30. This ignores the negative Z implied by a probability below 0.5.

15.87% = 1 - 0.8413 = P(Z < -1), so Z at Rs 430 is -1: (430 - mu)/sigma = -1 => mu = 430 + sigma. Also Z at Rs 490 is 2: (490 - mu)/sigma = 2 => 490 - mu = 2*sigma. Substituting: 490 - 430 - sigma = 2*sigma => 60 = 3*sigma => sigma = 20, mu = 450.

Assuming mu = (430 + 490)/2 = 460 (midpoint of the two cutoffs) and using only the upper equation: (490 - 460)/sigma = 2 => sigma = 15. The midpoint is not the mean unless the two Z-scores are equal in magnitude.
Treating the full X-range (490 - 430 = 60) as one standard deviation (confusing the sigma unit with the Z-distance of 3 sigma between the two cutoffs) gives sigma = 60.

explanation: The hidden step: 15.87% = 1 - 0.8413 = P(Z < -1), so the lower cutoff at Rs 430 corresponds to Z = -1, not +1. Writing the two Z-equations: (430 - mu)/sigma = -1 gives mu = 430 + sigma ... (i); (490 - mu)/sigma = 2 gives 490 - mu = 2*sigma ... (ii). Substituting (i) into (ii): 490 - 430 - sigma = 2*sigma => 60 = 3*sigma => sigma = 20 and mu = 450. Verify: (430 - 450)/20 = -1 and (490 - 450)/20 = 2, matching the given table values.

explanation_sections.punchline: The trap is reading 15.87% as Z = +1; recognising P(Z < -1) = 1 - P(Z < 1) leads to the two-equation system giving sigma = 20.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify model (normal), then map each probability to its Z-score. P(X < 430) = 0.1587 = 1 - 0.8413 = P(Z < -1), so Z_430 = -1. P(X < 490) = 0.9772 = P(Z < 2), so Z_490 = 2. Write Z-equations: mu - 430 = sigma (from Z = -1) and 490 - mu = 2*sigma (from Z = 2). Add the two equations: (490 - 430) = 3*sigma => 60 = 3*sigma => sigma = 20. Verify both cutoffs match.
explanation_sections.lesson: When a stated probability is below 0.5, its Z-score is negative; always convert using 1 - table_value before writing the standardisation equation.
explanation_sections.timing: About 110-130 seconds. The decisive trap is the sign of Z for the lower tail; once identified, the algebra is straightforward. Distractor Rs 30 is the most dangerous because it uses real numbers from the problem.
